verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the children of Israel that they put out of the camp every leper, and everyone who has an issue, and whoever is unclean by the dead.
Both you shall put male and female outside of the camp; that they not defile their camp, in the middle of which I dwell.”
The children of Israel did so, and put them outside of the camp; as Yahweh spoke to Moses, so did the children of Israel.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the children of Israel: ‘When a man or woman commits any sin that men commit, so as to trespass against Yahweh, and that soul is guilty;
then he shall confess his sin which he has done, and he shall make restitution for his guilt in full, and add to it the fifth part of it, and give it to him in respect of whom he has been guilty.

But if the man has no kinsman to whom restitution may be made for the guilt, the restitution for guilt which is made to Yahweh shall be the priest’s; besides the ram of the atonement, by which atonement shall be made for him.
Every heave offering of all the holy things of the children of Israel, which they present to the priest, shall be his.
Every man’s holy things shall be his: whatever any man gives the priest, it shall be his.’”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them: ‘If any man’s wife goes astray, and is unfaithful to him,
and a man lies with her carnally, and it is hidden from the eyes of her husband, and is kept close, and she is defiled, and there is no witness against her, and she isn’t taken in the act;
and the spirit of jealousy comes on him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she is defiled: or if the spirit of jealousy comes on him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she isn’t defiled:

then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and shall bring her offering for her: one tenth of an ephah  of barley meal. He shall pour no oil on it, nor put frankincense on it, for it is a meal offering of jealousy, a meal offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to memory.
The priest shall bring her near, and set her before Yahweh;
and the priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel; and of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle the priest shall take, and put it into the water.

The priest shall set the woman before Yahweh, and let the hair of the woman’s head go loose, and put the meal offering of memorial in her hands, which is the meal offering of jealousy. The priest shall have in his hand the water of bitterness that brings a curse.

The priest shall cause her to swear, and shall tell the woman, “If no man has lain with you, and if you haven’t gone aside to uncleanness, being under your husband, be free from this water of bitterness that brings a curse.
But if you have gone astray, being under your husband, and if you are defiled, and some man has lain with you besides your husband:”

then the priest shall cause the woman to swear with the oath of cursing, and the priest shall tell the woman, “Yahweh make you a curse and an oath among your people, when Yahweh allows your thigh to fall away, and your body to swell;
and this water that brings a curse will go into your bowels, and make your body swell, and your thigh fall away.” The woman shall say, “Amen, Amen.”
“‘The priest shall write these curses in a book, and he shall blot them out into the water of bitterness.
He shall make the woman drink the water of bitterness that causes the curse; and the water that causes the curse shall enter into her and become bitter.
The priest shall take the meal offering of jealousy out of the woman’s hand, and shall wave the meal offering before Yahweh, and bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take a handful of the meal offering, as its memorial, and burn it on the altar, and afterward shall make the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, then it shall happen, if she is defiled, and has committed a trespass against her husband, that the water that causes the curse will enter into her and become bitter, and her body will swell, and her thigh will fall away: and the woman will be a curse among her people.
If the woman isn’t defiled, but is clean; then she shall be free, and shall conceive offspring.
“‘This is the law of jealousy, when a wife, being under her husband, goes astray, and is defiled;
or when the spirit of jealousy comes on a man, and he is jealous of his wife; then he shall set the woman before Yahweh, and the priest shall execute on her all this law.
The man shall be free from iniquity, and that woman shall bear her iniquity.’”

footnotes.content: Again Yahweh speaks through Moses. The people are learning that holiness isn't just inner attitude—it shapes how we live together. The Lord cares about both the spiritual and the practical, the altar and the camp boundaries.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three kinds of separation: the leper, the issue (the ritually unclean), the one defiled by death. Each represents a real brokenness—body, blood, proximity to loss. The Lord names them plainly. There's mercy in honesty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "In the middle of which I dwell." Not in a tent only, but in the midst. Separation isn't exile from the Lord's presence—it's preparation for return to it. The boundary exists because He dwells there, and He is holy and jealous for His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They obeyed. It would have been hard—sending out the sick, the grieving, the broken. But the people trusted what Moses spoke. That obedience, however costly, plants the seed of covenant faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A new word begins. Now we turn from separation-for-holiness to something deeper: what sin does between us and God. The law shifts from the boundary to the conscience.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Any sin that men commit"—not just the ceremonial, but the moral. Trespass against Yahweh. The smallest dishonesty, the hidden taking, the broken promise—He marks it. And guilt isn't a feeling; it's a real debt owed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Confession and restitution, plus a fifth part more. Not just return what was taken—restore it generously. The extra fifth speaks of genuine sorrow, not mere mechanics. Yahweh loves the cheerful restorer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When there's no one left to restore to—no kinsman, no heir—the debt goes to the priest and the atonement ram. Even the orphaned sin has a path to Yahweh. His mercy is always there to receive what we owe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Heave offerings"—the lifted gift, the priestly portion. It's a small word on a practical matter: the priest's livelihood. But look: the priest who mediates the people's sin also receives their generosity. Trust flows two ways.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Whatever any man gives the priest, it shall be his." A holy gift becomes the giver's provision. The Lord builds this into the covenant: those who serve the altar eat from the altar. Faithfulness and provision are woven together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A third time: "Yahweh spoke to Moses." Three teachings in one chapter—separation, restitution, and now marriage. Each touches the covenant's nerve: How do we keep ourselves fit for His presence?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "If any man's wife goes astray." The word is stark. Not mere misunderstanding, but unfaithfulness—a breach. The marriage covenant echoes the covenant with Yahweh. Both require faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hidden, kept close, unwitnessed. She is defiled in the secret place where no one saw. Yet Yahweh sees. The law acknowledges what human courts cannot—hidden sin is still sin. And it grieves Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The spirit of jealousy. Whether defiled or not, the suspicion comes. Jealousy can torment even where no wrong exists. The law makes room for this: we aren't always sure, but we can seek the truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "A meal offering of jealousy, a meal offering of memorial." Barley—the grain of the common, not wheat of the grand. No oil, no frankincense. Plain, humble, bringing iniquity to remembrance. Even jealousy can be brought before Yahweh with truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The woman is brought before Yahweh, not before the crowd. Her case comes first to Him. Even in her shame or innocence, she stands in His sight. The Lord sees.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Holy water, dust from the tabernacle floor. Water speaks of cleansing; dust of humbling. The elements of her trial are woven from the very ground of Yahweh's dwelling. The trial itself is an encounter with His holiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Her hair let loose, the meal offering in her hands, the water of bitterness in the priest's hands. Everything speaks: vulnerability, her offering, the consequence she must face. She stands exposed before Yahweh's justice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The oath of innocence. If she hasn't strayed, she may drink freely and be clear. There is a way out—truthfulness. The Lord always leaves room for the innocent to stand clean.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But if she has gone astray, now the words are spoken. The truth is named. There's a moment when cover falls away and the reality stands bare before Yahweh and her husband both.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The oath of curse. Yahweh Himself is called upon as witness and judge. The consequences are named plainly. This is severe, but mercy shows through: the truth is allowed to come forward, not remain hidden forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Amen, Amen." She speaks the curse upon herself if guilty, accepting Yahweh's judgment. There is a courage in choosing truth, even when truth brings shame. The double amen is her binding word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest writes the curse in a book and blots it into the water. Written word, erased, absorbed. It's as if the curse is given form, witnessed, then swallowed into her very drink. Nothing is left hidden.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She drinks. The water that causes the curse enters her. If her oath is false, she bears the consequence. There is a stark honesty here: choose truth, or accept what follows. The law offers no middle ground.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The meal offering is waved before Yahweh, the priestly gesture of presenting the offering. Even in judgment, the act of offering continues. Yahweh receives it. The ceremony holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A handful burned, memorial rising as smoke. Then she drinks again. The offering ascends; she receives. Even in her trial, she is held within the frame of worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If she is guilty, the consequence comes. Her body bears the mark. Trespass against her husband is a trespass against the covenant itself, and the Lord does not hide His judgment. Consequences are written in the flesh.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If she is clean, she shall be free and conceive offspring. Innocence leads to blessing. The Lord grants her restoration, fertility, life itself. Faithfulness and fruitfulness are bound together in His sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "This is the law of jealousy." It is law—fixed, binding, meant to govern the community's life. Even the difficult cases have their place in Yahweh's order. There is wisdom in structure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When jealousy rises in a man's heart, he brings the case to the priest, who executes the whole law. The priest stands between suspicion and judgment, order-keeper between covenant-mate and covenant-breaker.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The man shall be free from iniquity, and that woman shall bear her iniquity." Looking back from a longer road, I see how the law holds both: the accuser goes clean, the guilty soul carries consequence. Truth demands a cost. Readers today hear an echo: Yahweh's justice holds all things to account, and we cannot hide forever from what we've done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
